title: Relative-modular cocycle and resolvent Cook bridge
question: Can a phase-local relative modular cocycle on a resolvent core replace the all-history norm estimate by a summable boundary Cook criterion, while preserving both orientations and the Hamiltonian generator?
method: Resum the nested-volume difference into U_prime,H(t)=exp(i t H_prime) exp(-i t H) before taking any norm, and derive the ordered cocycle equation on the common form/resolvent core.
Apply a phase-local conditional expectation to [B,R_z(A)] before the estimate so that the bulk cancels and only boundary shells remain.
Use the two-sided fixed-beta mixture GNS/BKM norm for the cocycle and its modular derivative, with the adjoint orientation checked separately.
Target a source-, cutoff-, volume- and shape-uniform l1 shell coefficient; integrate it by Cook/Duhamel to obtain direct D and delta-D Cauchy on the resolvent core.
Use the resolvent identity for product/inverse closure and only then test the common Hamiltonian generator and phasewise OS/KMS identification.
Keep the route conditional and retire it only if the actual Q3LOCK boundary coefficient is non-summable or the resolvent core is not invariant.
finding: A distinct proof decomposition is now recorded: relative-cocycle resummation and phase-local state-weighted conditioning occur before the thermodynamic estimate. This avoids the raw point-norm Weyl carrier and the per-history absolute counting debt, but the actual Q3LOCK BKM boundary estimate and shell summability are not proved.
decision_reason: The route changes the load-bearing object from every split history to one relative modular cocycle and creates two precise falsifiable lemmas (phase-local BKM boundary control and l1 shell summability). It is a route advance only; no mathematical parent gate is closed until those Q3LOCK inputs and the embedding/group-law obligations are proved.

adversarial_review.check: The ordered product and its adjoint must be differentiated explicitly; a commuting perturbation surrogate is not allowed.
The quartic boundary polynomial is unbounded, so a form/resolvent core and a verified perturbation domain are required before any Cook integral is legal.
Only the exact difference of identically normalized nested Hamiltonians cancels the bulk; the boundary halo and embedding convention must be enumerated.
Two-sided GNS convergence is weaker than point norm and does not automatically produce a representation-independent C-star action.
Finite R-384 profiles and static tails do not imply an l1 boundary coefficient; failure in one orientation must stop this route.
A successful cocycle limit would still require Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS identification, a sector gap and the independent C6/Sector-A/Pre-A interfaces.

formal_integration.lean: not applicable at route-design stage; R377 scalar identity is reused

next_action: First derive the finite ordered cocycle and resolvent-core commutator identities on the actual Q3 edge/square fixtures; then test whether the phase-local BKM shell coefficient is summable in both orientations. A finite pass must add a primary/independent/Lean package, while a non-summable coefficient is recorded as a route-specific obstruction.
boundary: Claim-nonbearing route design only. It proves no Q3 boundary coefficient, cocycle summability, direct D/delta-D Cauchy theorem, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The cocycle/resolvent bridge is a falsifiable idea, not a proof closure. The hard Q3LOCK shell estimate, cutoff removal and compatible spatial embeddings remain open.
